newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH committed to Latin America.
newsitem.headline: CHH committed to Latin America.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Chief Executive John Faraci said on Wednesday the forestry company remained committed to Latin America, despite legal difficulties with its Chilean associate, Copec.

Faraci told the New Zealand Investment Conference in Auckland that the company's initial investment in Chile totalled US$10 million 10 years ago, expanding to US$600 million today, representing 20 percent of CHH's total assets.
"We are committed to expanding our presence in Latin America through our investment in Copec, and in particular working closely with its forestry subsidiary, Arauco," Faraci said.

Faraci said Copec's forestry sector complemented CHH's, the two countries sharing 70 percent of the world's radiata pine plantation forests. "By working together, Arauco and CHH have the potential to be world leaders in the major global markets," Faraci said.
Copec is one of Chile's largest industrial companies and Arauco represents 66 percent of its assets.
Copec manages 700,000 hectares of, and is one of the world's low cost producers of, market pulp.
"Clearly, our investment in Copec is substantial and strategically important to us. We are in Chile for the long term," he said.
CHH has been in a long running legal dispute with its Chilean partner, Angelini Group.

"As 50/50 partners in Los Andes that controls 60 percent of Copec, we are committed to becoming a more active equal partner in our joint venture. We are convinced that working closely with our partner, we can create more value for all Copec shareholders and CHH shareholders," Faraci said.
